title: Quaternionic Hermitian Band Geometry in Four Dimensions: Realization on $S^4$ and Obstruction on $T^4$
authors: Dongju Hwang, Minjae Yu, Gil Young Cho
abstract: We establish a realization-obstruction dichotomy for quaternionic Hermitian band geometry in four-dimensional parameter spaces: the minimal-charge lowest Landau level on $S^{4}$ provides a global realization, whereas an everywhere nondegenerate saturated realization induced by a single occupied quaternionic band is obstructed on $T^{4}$. An antiunitary symmetry $\mathcal{J}$ satisfying $\mathcal{J}^{2}=-1$ makes the occupied doublet a quaternionic band. Within this setting, we formulate the quaternionic Wirtinger inequality as a band-geometric bound involving the quantum metric and the second Chern density. At every nondegenerate saturation point, the canonical geometry of the quaternionic projective space pulls back to a compatible quaternionic structure on the parameter space; if these conditions hold everywhere, the parameter space acquires quaternionic Hermitian band geometry. On $S^{4}$, we express the minimal-charge states as quaternionic Perelomov coherent states and establish everywhere nondegenerate saturation, thereby realizing quaternionic Hermitian band geometry. On $T^{4}$, by contrast, a minimal four-band system saturates the inequality everywhere, but topology forces the quantum metric to become degenerate somewhere, obstructing a globally induced quaternionic structure. An explicit lattice Dirac Hamiltonian exhibits this obstruction. Adding unoccupied bands cannot remove this obstruction when the inequality is saturated everywhere, since the image of any nondegenerate saturated projector remains confined to a fixed $\mathbb{H}P^{1}$. These results provide a symmetry-aware framework for non-Abelian band geometry and show how parameter-space topology constrains the global realization of quaternionic Hermitian band geometry.
summary: This theoretical work investigates quaternionic Hermitian band geometry in 4D parameter spaces, using the quaternionic Wirtinger inequality as a diagnostic tool. It demonstrates that while the geometry is globally realized on the 4-sphere ($S^4$), topological constraints prevent its global realization on the 4-torus ($T^4$). This highlights a fundamental link between topology and the realizability of advanced geometric structures in electronic band theory.
main_problem: The paper establishes a realization-obstruction dichotomy for quaternionic Hermitian band geometry in four-dimensional parameter spaces.
main_result: Global realization is achieved on $S^4$ using minimal-charge Landau levels, but the geometry is obstructed on $T^4$ due to topological constraints forcing metric degeneracy.
method: The authors formulate the quaternionic Wirtinger inequality as a band-geometric bound, comparing its saturation conditions on $S^4$ versus $T^4$.
model_or_system: The study analyzes the geometry derived from occupied doublets forming a 'quaternionic band' in a four-dimensional parameter space, contrasting the sphere ($S^4$) with the torus ($T^4$).
key_observables: Quantum metric, second Chern density, and the saturation of the quaternionic Wirtinger inequality.
important_parameters: The dimensionality of the parameter space (4D), the nature of the symmetry ($\mathcal{J}$), and the band structure (minimal charge/four-band system).
main_assumptions: The framework extends 2D Kähler band geometry to 4D, and the analysis relies on the properties of the occupied subspace being preserved by an antiunitary symmetry $J$.
figures_summary: The notes do not describe specific figures, but reference calculations involving the Berry connection, curvature, and the explicit lattice Dirac Hamiltonian on $T^4$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the quaternionic Wirtinger inequality, then applying it to the $S^4$ case (showing realization), and finally contrasting this with the $T^4$ case (showing obstruction).
why_interesting: The work provides a powerful, symmetry-aware framework for understanding how global topology constrains the realizability of complex geometric structures (like quaternionic Kähler geometry) in condensed matter band theory.
